record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the stochastic M/G/k queue with arrivals over time, what is the mean-response-time performance of SRPT-k outside the heavy-traffic regime?

evidence.quote: Outside of heavy traffic, understanding when SRPT-k is optimal and analyzing its performance are both big open problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the M/G/k queue: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λ, each job has an i.i.d. service requirement drawn from a general distribution G with finite mean, and there are k ≥ 2 identical servers. Let ρ = λE[G]/k < 1 denote the load. Under the SRPT-k (Shortest Remaining Processing Time for k servers) scheduling policy, at every instant the k jobs in the system with the smallest remaining service requirements are placed in service (preempting jobs of larger remaining size when necessary); if fewer than k jobs are present, all are served. The response time T of a job is the time from its arrival until its departure.

Provide a quantitative analysis of the mean response time E[T] of the M/G/k queue under SRPT-k that is valid outside the heavy-traffic regime (i.e., for general values of ρ ∈ (0,1), not only the limit ρ → 1). In particular, characterize E[T] (e.g., via tight closed-form bounds, asymptotic expansions, or exact expressions) as a function of λ, k, and the service-time distribution G, and determine the regimes (in terms of ρ, k, and properties of G) in which SRPT-k is optimal or near-optimal among all scheduling policies for minimizing E[T].
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Grosof–Scully–Harchol-Balter, SIGMETRICS 2018) provided the first stochastic mean-response-time bounds for SRPT-k and established asymptotic optimality in the heavy-traffic limit ρ → 1. Outside heavy traffic, only heavy-traffic-based approximations and bounds exist; precise characterization of E[T] and identification of when SRPT-k is exactly optimal remain unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: SRPT for Multiserver Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Multiserver SRPT has asymptotically optimal mean response time in the heavy-traffic limit, using a combination of stochastic and worst-case techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results establish heavy-traffic asymptotic optimality of SRPT-k but do not characterize its performance outside heavy traffic.

status_evidence.title: Heavy-traffic analysis of mean response time under SRPT
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes growth rate of mean response time under SRPT in M/GI/1 in the heavy-traffic limit.
status_evidence.claim: Available analyses concentrate on heavy-traffic regimes.
